Name: Requiring analyses of cooling towers associated with Legionnaires’ disease clusters.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to requiring analyses of cooling towers associated with Legionnaires’ disease clusters

History.Description: This Introduction was Introduced by Council
This Introduction was Referred to Comm by Council to the Committee on Health

Summary: This bill would require that the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH), in consultation with the Department of Buildings (DOB), conduct an analysis to identify the common characteristics of cooling towers associated with each Legionnaires’ disease cluster and to issue recommendations to prevent cooling towers from causing future Legionnaires’ disease clusters.
Text:
Be it enacted by the Council as follows:
      
      
      Section 1. Section 17-194.1 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new subdivision n to read as follows:
      n. Cooling tower analysis. 1. Within 3 months after the department determines that a Legionnaires' disease cluster has ended, the commissioner, in consultation with the commissioner of buildings, shall conduct an analysis to identify the common characteristics of cooling towers associated with the Legionnaires' disease cluster. The analysis shall, at a minimum, consider:
      (a) Each cooling tower's manufacturer, commission date, design, construction, condition, placement on roof, and proximity to vents;
      (b) Maintenance, cleaning and disinfection practices and adherence to the building's maintenance program and plan, as set forth in subdivision c of this section; 
      (c) The height of each building associated with the disease cluster; and
      (d) Other factors that may contribute to the growth or dispersion of legionella bacteria. 
      2. Within 30 days of completing each cooling tower analysis, the commissioner, in consultation with the commissioner of buildings, shall issue, and post on the department's website, a report outlining the department's findings and recommendations for preventing cooling towers from causing future Legionnaires' disease clusters, which may include changes to:
      (a) Cooling tower design, construction, and placement practices and requirements;
      (b) Cooling tower maintenance, inspection, and testing practices and requirements; and
      (c) The New York city building code, New York city mechanical code, New York city health code, and other relevant New York city codes or local laws. 
      � 2. This local law takes effect immediately.
